description:
Responsibilities:
Definition, evolution, and development of a new web platform for the management and control of non-domestic discharges in La Rioja, aimed at replacing a legacy Microsoft Access solution and centralising information within a single registry.

Due to the absence of a Product Owner, I also took on product-related responsibilities and direct client management, including requirements gathering, functional definition of the system, backlog prioritisation, delivery planning, and continuous validation of functional evolution.

The application brings together the management of authorisations, inspections, laboratory analyses, case tracking, and discharge fee calculations, improving traceability, interoperability across organisations, and user and operational control. It is one of the most relevant projects of my recent career because of its functional complexity, its direct impact on public administration, and the high level of end-to-end ownership involved.
proyect_1.name: Project: Central Registry of Non-Domestic Discharges - CARE Wastewater Control Center

description:
Responsibilities:
Development of a solution focused on the monitoring, operation, and maintenance of meteorological radar systems, providing a centralised view of radar status, variables, alarms, and availability indicators.

The platform combined visualisation and analytics capabilities with document management, inventory, and maintenance features, improving operational control and traceability across the radar ecosystem.

In this project, I led a key architectural decision: adopting ThingsBoard as the foundation of the IoT visualisation and operations system. I was a pioneer within the organisation in evaluating and introducing it, validating its fit for a critical meteorological environment and taking advantage of its native dashboards, telemetry, rules, and APIs to reduce technical risk, cost, and delivery time.

My role focused especially on integration and backend architecture, defining how data flowed into ThingsBoard, how services were structured, and how the solution evolved towards a more modular, maintainable, and traceable model. In parallel, I promoted knowledge transfer through internal video tutorials to support adoption by other teams.
proyect_2.name: Project: C-OM (Operations and Monitoring Centre) - AEMET

introduction.title: Sergio Asensio Puyuelo
content: Welcome to my website!

I am Sergio Asensio, a Technical Lead and Software Architect with a degree in Mathematics from the University of Zaragoza. I have more than 10 years of experience developing software solutions and over 4 years of specialization in projects related to the water and environmental sector.

I currently lead development projects and teams, participating in the entire software lifecycle: from requirements gathering and architecture design to production deployment. I act as a bridge between business, clients, and technical teams, helping transform needs into solutions that deliver value and can be maintained and evolved over time.

innovation.title: Innovation
content: Throughout my time as a Technical Lead, I have played an active role in the company's internal technical standardization, promoting reusable project skeletons in Node.js, Angular, and Flutter, implementing GitLab CI continuous integration pipelines, and fully containerizing applications to standardize environments and accelerate deliveries.

I have also been a pioneer in the evaluation, adoption, and implementation of ThingsBoard within the organization, validating its use in real IoT monitoring projects and encouraging its internal reuse. In parallel, I created video tutorials and training materials to accelerate team onboarding and facilitate knowledge transfer.

Additionally, I have contributed to the definition of technical standards, methodologies, and development guidelines aimed at improving collaboration across teams and maintaining a consistent way of working.

about_me.title: About Me
content: I am a highly persistent person, and that is probably the quality that best defines me professionally. I enjoy taking on new challenges, constantly learning, and finding solutions to problems that initially seem difficult to solve. The more challenging and unfamiliar a project is, the more motivated I am to understand it and make it succeed.

I have always placed great importance on the foundations of a project. I like to take the time to think things through, establish a solid base, and ensure that early decisions allow for sustainable growth in the future. Likewise, I believe the best solutions come from a strong team: committed, organized people with shared goals who support each other and move forward together.

I hope this website helps you get to know me a little better and that you enjoy exploring it as much as I enjoyed designing and developing it. If you would like to learn more about my experience, projects, or simply talk about technology, feel free to get in touch through the link below:

technologies.title: Architecture & Technologies
content: Throughout my career, I have participated in the design and development of software architectures, web applications, mobile applications, data platforms, and IoT solutions, contributing to projects of different sizes, industries, and levels of complexity.
I have worked with technologies such as Java, Angular, React, Salesforce, Flutter, Node.js, Python, and ThingsBoard, both independently and as part of multidisciplinary teams.

My experience covers areas such as full-stack development, data modeling, software architecture, reusable component design, systems integration, Docker containerization, and cloud deployments on platforms such as OpenShift, Azure, and Heroku, always focusing on solutions that are maintainable, understandable, and capable of evolving alongside business needs.

agile.title: Agility & Team Management
content: I enjoy working in an organized manner and maintaining constant communication with clients and teams. For this reason, I rely on agile methodologies such as Scrum and Kanban, using roadmaps and iterative planning to maintain a clear vision of project direction and priorities.

I believe that a good solution should not only work but also be easy to maintain and evolve. To achieve this, I apply practices such as Gitflow, Pull Requests, code reviews, testing, Clean Code, SOLID principles, and Continuous Integration, while also leveraging Artificial Intelligence tools to streamline certain tasks and improve productivity.

I also encourage clients to have access to testing environments where they can validate progress and provide early feedback, fostering continuous collaboration and ensuring alignment between business needs and the delivered solution.

personal_projects_page.intro: This section gathers public GitHub projects that show how I design reusable foundations, structure technical decisions, and prepare products for real delivery.

flutter_base_app.architecture: The project is split into app, core, and feature layers. Authentication is handled separately from the shell, while top-level navigation is state-driven through AppBloc instead of relying only on route pushes.
highlights: Reusable starter template for API-driven Flutter applications.
Built-in authentication flow, modular shell navigation, and global request feedback.
Prepared for localization, environment-based configuration, and version display in the UI.
Includes unit, widget, and integration testing support together with SonarQube and GitLab CI stages.
flutter_base_app.overview: A reusable Flutter base application intended to accelerate the start of new products. It provides the technical groundwork for apps that need authentication, modular navigation, shared infrastructure, and a cleaner separation between shell behavior and domain features.
flutter_base_app.quality: The repository includes test coverage support, integration tests, static analysis, SonarQube configuration, and a CI pipeline with dependency, analyze, test, build, and sonar stages.
flutter_base_app.stack: Flutter and Dart with flutter_bloc, bloc, equatable, http, http_interceptor, flutter_secure_storage, shared_preferences, flutter_dotenv, get_it, loader_overlay, intl, and package_info_plus.
flutter_base_app.subtitle: Reusable Flutter starter template for API-driven apps
flutter_base_app.title: flutter-base-app

node_base_app.architecture: The backend follows a bootstrap, core, and features split. It separates routes, controllers, services, repositories, DTOs, and schemas clearly, while keeping authentication, RBAC, OpenAPI exposure, and database assets organized by responsibility.
highlights: Reusable backend skeleton for API products built with TypeScript and Express.
Includes JWT authentication with refresh token rotation and RBAC authorization.
Provides CRUD reference modules, OpenAPI exposure, Docker support, and PostgreSQL integration through Objection.js and Knex as the ORM/persistence layer.
Comes with integration-style API tests, coverage tooling, and GitLab CI stages for build, test, sonar, and ZAP.
node_base_app.overview: A reusable Node.js base application designed to accelerate the creation of structured backend APIs. It establishes a clean technical foundation for real projects that need authentication, authorization, modular business features, database migrations, and consistent delivery tooling.
node_base_app.quality: The repository includes linting, formatting, Mocha and Chai API tests, NYC coverage reporting, SonarQube support, and a CI pipeline with dependency, build, test, sonar, and zap stages.
node_base_app.stack: Node.js, TypeScript, Express, Objection.js, Knex, PostgreSQL, TypeDI, jsonwebtoken, bcrypt, cookie-parser, dotenv, Winston, Mocha, Chai, NYC, ESLint, and Prettier.
node_base_app.subtitle: Reusable Node.js backend skeleton for API-driven applications
node_base_app.title: node-base-app

sergio_asensio_cv_reborn.architecture: The frontend is organized around core, features, shared, and store areas. It uses a shell-style navigation model, standalone Angular components, NgRx for module state, and bilingual content driven through translation files.
highlights: Angular portfolio application focused on presenting professional profile, curriculum, and personal projects.
Includes responsive top and side navigation, bilingual content, and modular standalone feature sections.
Uses Angular Material, Bootstrap, NgRx, and ngx-translate to balance structure, UI consistency, and maintainability.
Prepared for Docker packaging and Cloudflare deployment with SPA routing support.
sergio_asensio_cv_reborn.overview: A rebuilt version of my personal CV website, created as a maintainable frontend application rather than a static presentation page. It serves both as my public portfolio and as a practical reference for how I structure Angular frontends with modular features, shared state, responsive navigation, and multilingual content.
sergio_asensio_cv_reborn.quality: The project includes unit tests with Karma and Jasmine, linting and formatting workflows, standalone component architecture, and deployment preparation through Docker, Nginx, and Wrangler.
sergio_asensio_cv_reborn.stack: Angular 21, TypeScript, Angular Material, CDK, Bootstrap 5, Font Awesome, NgRx Store and Effects, ngx-translate, Karma, Jasmine, ESLint, Prettier, Docker, and Cloudflare Wrangler.
sergio_asensio_cv_reborn.subtitle: Angular portfolio frontend for CV, experience, and personal project showcase
sergio_asensio_cv_reborn.title: sergio-asensio-cv-reborn
